newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber end mostly lower on slowing cash.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber end mostly lower on slowing cash.

text.p: Reports that cash lumber trade again turned slow after recent price gains weighed on CME lumber futures in light dealings, traders said.
Lumber closed $1.20 per tbf lower to $2.70 higher with only September up and May off most at $383.80. July ended $0.80 lower at $375.80 per tbf.

Futures opened up to technical resistance above $388 per tbf after filling a gap in the charts on buying prompted by a higher cash quote. A surge of heavy lumber exports from Canada has not materialized at the start of the new quota year, which also lent early support. But prices slipped as cash trade slowed, traders said.
Retailers bought some wood and mills raised asking prices but there was no followthrough demand to keep prices trending much higher, sources said.
Random Lengths early Friday quoted cash spruce at $383 per tbf, up $5 from Friday and $16 above last midweek, partly from the Canadian "wall of wood" failing to develop, they said.
